cues.text: For next week, I’d like you to undertake a piece of research in preparation for writing your final essay.
cues.speaker: Professor

cues.text: In order to gain top marks, you must include a range of primary, secondary, and tertiary sources.
cues.speaker: Professor

cues.text: Are there any questions?
cues.speaker: Professor

cues.text: Yes, Professor, I have a question. We haven’t yet covered how to undertake this sort of research in much depth, and I’m a little unsure of what you want us to do.
cues.speaker: Douglas

cues.text: In telling us to include primary sources, do you mean you want us to design and distribute a questionnaire, analysing the results?
cues.speaker: Douglas

cues.text: You could design a questionnaire, but you’ll soon find that distributing a questionnaire on such a large scale is somewhat troublesome.
cues.speaker: Professor

cues.text: We couldn’t possibly expect you to do it effectively as an individual university student without the necessary resources.
cues.speaker: Professor

cues.text: No, ideally I would like you to form one or two focus groups, and  interview them.
cues.speaker: Professor

cues.text: This will provide you with a more qualitative approach.
cues.speaker: Professor

cues.text: If your strengths lie in mathematics, please by all means take a more quantitative approach, but this will be more strenuous and time consuming, and isn’t entirely necessary for the purpose of this study.
cues.speaker: Professor

cues.text: Professor, you haven’t told us what our project is about.
cues.speaker: Jane

cues.text: Do we get to choose our own topic based on the previous study?
cues.speaker: Jane

cues.text: No, I’m afraid not. This will be a strictly  Australian study;
cues.speaker: Professor

cues.text: however, you can choose which angle you’d like to take, so long as it remains within the realm of anthropology.
cues.speaker: Professor

cues.text: Does anyone have any questions specifically about the formation of the focus groups?
cues.speaker: Professor

cues.text: ’ve had several emails about this, and I’d like to address it now.
cues.speaker: Professor

cues.text: My study is related to growing up in Australia, and the question of nature versus nurture.
cues.speaker: Douglas

cues.text: I’ve gathered more than two hundred school children who would be happy to participate in a focus group.
cues.speaker: Douglas

cues.text: Do you think we’ll need to include that many participants in a focus group?
cues.speaker: Douglas

cues.text: Blimey, Douglas, well done for finding that many willing children, but you definitely don’t need that many for the study you’re going to undertake.
cues.speaker: Professor

cues.text: I’d say you need no more than five children per group, and no more than three groups, so fifteen children altogether.
cues.speaker: Professor

cues.text: You definitely need to control the group size in order to generate a meaningful dialogue.
cues.speaker: Professor

cues.text: OK, if it’s useful, I’ll try and do it...
cues.speaker: Douglas

cues.text: I appreciate your enthusiasm for the project, but there are plenty of different ways to gather data, and I’m sure that if you look hard enough, you’ll find someone who has conducted almost the exact same research in the past.
cues.speaker: Professor

cues.text: My advice for you is don’t be too ambitious, and try to include as much information about various people or sectors.
cues.speaker: Professor

cues.text: For those who haven’t ever collected original data before, what do you suggest we do?
cues.speaker: Jane

cues.text: I would suggest that you read accounts from other people who have undertaken such research to see what advice they can give.
cues.speaker: Professor

cues.text: I would also encourage you to read Chapter Eight in the course textbook, which should give you a good introduction to collecting data.
cues.speaker: Professor

cues.text: Moreover, you should try to practice using the data table provided in your course handbook.
cues.speaker: Professor

cues.text: By now you should have read at least six or seven books giving quite detailed instruction on how to go about collecting data.
cues.speaker: Professor

cues.text: Professor, I don’t know about everyone else, but I m having trouble reading the books.
cues.speaker: Douglas

cues.text: I had a really big assignment for another course and I’ve been spending all my time on that.
cues.speaker: Douglas

cues.text: Jane, have you read all the books the professor mentioned?
cues.speaker: Douglas

cues.text: Well, my trouble is getting hold of the books. I’ve been to the library several times, but all the books are out.
cues.speaker: Jane

cues.text: Sounds like you should have started borrowing books a bit earlier.
cues.speaker: Professor

cues.text: Yes, I should have. But I got several ones from my friend a couple of days ago.
cues.speaker: Jane

cues.text: I just skimmed through them, and don’t remember a lot of the information.
cues.speaker: Jane

cues.text: But now let’s look at these things. We’ll need to start thinking about which ones we’ll definitely want to do for the project.
cues.speaker: Jane

cues.text: Okay. The first one here is the final report.
cues.speaker: Douglas

cues.text: If you like, we can work together on the research and data-collection side of the project, and doing the final write-up?
cues.speaker: Jane

cues.text: Cool. That sounds good. I’m not sure how much I’d be able to contribute considering I haven’t had a chance to read the course material.
cues.speaker: Douglas

cues.text: But I should be able to prepare some sheets and a list of questions that can be used during the focus group sessions.
cues.speaker: Douglas

cues.text: That sounds appropriate. I think so too.
cues.speaker: Jane

cues.text: Do you think we’ll need to write a letter to send to the participants, telling them the time and place for the interviews?
cues.speaker: Douglas

cues.text: Positive. I can take care of that.
cues.speaker: Jane

cues.text: Well, that’s great.
cues.speaker: Douglas

cues.text: I should also include a document for them to sign saying that they’re happy to be voice-recorded.
cues.speaker: Jane

cues.text: Oh yes, of course. I forgot about the transcript.
cues.speaker: Douglas

cues.text: That’ll likely be a big job, so let’s do half each, I’ll do one of the groups and you can do the other. Okay?
cues.speaker: Douglas

cues.text: Sounds like a plan!
cues.speaker: Jane
